question: A network administrator must configure an extra keyring in Cisco UCS Manager. The key must provide a high level of encryption and secure authentication when users use the web interface. Which configuration command set must be applied to meet these requirements?
options:
set https keyring kring7984
set https cipher-suite-mode high
set https tls-protocol tls1-2
commit-buffer

set https keyring kring7984
set https cipher-suite-mode high
set https ssl-protocol tls1-2
commit-buffer

set https keyring kring7984
set https cipher-suite-mode secure
set https ssl-protocol tls1-2
commit-buffer

set https keyring kring7984
set https cipher-suite-mode secure
set https tls-protocol tls1-2
commit-buffer
theory: Hardening Cisco UCS Manager's HTTPS management interface requires binding a keyring (which supplies the certificate/key material) to the HTTPS service, restricting the negotiated cipher suite to a high-security set with cipher-suite-mode high, and pinning the protocol version with set https ssl-protocol tls1-2 - note UCS Manager CLI uses the keyword 'ssl-protocol', not 'tls-protocol', for this setting. Together these commands prevent weak ciphers or older TLS/SSL versions from being negotiated for management sessions. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 19 - Securing UCS Management, HTTPS hardening)
